title: Ex 7.1 (⇐, by contrapositive) · If 3x + 5 is odd, then x is even
prompt: Let $x$ be an integer. Exercise 7.1 says $x$ is even if and only if $3x + 5$ is odd. This problem is one direction of that if-and-only-if: prove that if $3x + 5$ is odd, then $x$ is even. Use contrapositive proof: show that if $x$ is odd, then $3x + 5$ is even. (The forward (⇒) direction is a separate problem.)
answer_format: A structured proof: let, case, expr and witness steps (notes optional). No final answer box.
hints: The contrapositive is: if x is not even (so odd), then 3x + 5 is not odd (so even).
solution: Contrapositive: if $x$ is odd, then $3x + 5$ is even.
Suppose $x$ is odd, so $x = 2a + 1$. Then $3x + 5 = 6a + 8 = 2(3a + 4)$, which is even.
So if $3x + 5$ is odd, then $x$ is even. $\blacksquare$
